answer: The Four Seasons (Le quattro stagioni) was composed by the Italian Baroque composer Antonio Vivaldi [1][2]. It's a set of four violin concertos, one for each season, and each has three movements in a fast-slow-fast pattern [1][2]. Vivaldi published them in 1725 in Amsterdam, as the first four concertos of his Op. 8 collection, Il cimento dell'armonia e dell'inventione [1][2]. He probably wrote them a few years earlier, around 1718–1723, while he was working at the court in Mantua [2]. Each concerto comes with a sonnet describing the scene the music paints. Nobody knows who wrote the sonnets, though Vivaldi himself may have [2]. The name "The Four Seasons" is also used by other works, such as Astor Piazzolla's Four Seasons of Buenos Aires and Max Richter's recomposition, but it usually means Vivaldi's piece.

sources.title: 'The Four Seasons': A Guide To Vivaldi's Radical Violin Concertos
